newsitem.title: india: CRICKET-CRONJE STAGES WALK-OFF DURING INDIA TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CRONJE STAGES WALK-OFF DURING INDIA TEST.

text.p: South Africa captain Hansie Cronje took his players off the field during the first test against India on Friday after spinner Paul Adams was hit by a stone thrown from the crowd.
Adams, fielding on the boundary, was pelted with fruit and paper darts. But when he was hit by a stone, Cronje showed it to the umpires and promptly took his players off the field.
They stayed in the pavilion for 10 minutes before returning to complete the final session.
The incident marred an intriguing third day which saw India close on 172 for seven in their second innings, an overall lead of 151.
On a pitch which has been awkward throughout and has been helping the spinners, the game was superbly poised for an exciting finish.

The Indians, however, must thank their debutant V.V.S. Laxman for that position. Not only did he make a fighting 50 not out -- his maiden test half-century -- but also, in partnership with Anil Kumble, he rescued them from the perilous position of 124 for seven.
The South African fast bowlers did the damage, Allan Donald leading the hunt with three for 32 as the Indian top order caved in.

Trailing by 21 on the first innings after a fine 67 not out from Fanie de Villiers had helped South Africa to reach 244, the Indians were rocked by a fiery opening spell from Donald. Both Indian openers were back in the pavilion before they had wiped out the deficit.
Sanjay Manjrekar edged an outswinger to Andrew Hudson in the slips while Nayan Mongia snicked a catch to wicketkeeper Dave Richardson.
South Africa then claimed the crucial wicket of Indian skipper Sachin Tendulkar for seven just as he looked like getting into his stride with a rasping offside boundary off de Villiers.
The roars of applause turned to shocked silence a few deliveries later as Tendulkar spooned an innocuous Brian McMillan delivery to Jonty Rhodes at point.

Rahul Dravid, with 34, and Mohammed Azharuddin, 24, briefly looked like taking the fight to the South Africans as they added 44 for the fourth wicket but Donald had Azharuddin caught by McMillan and off-spinner Pat Symcox accounted for Dravid.
Earlier, de Villiers made the highest score of the match as he and Donald added 60 for the ninth wicket to take South Africa from 202 for eight overnight to 244 all out.
